title: Claude's new mobile app updates are here
format_note: On-camera presenter narrates a release roundup; cream UI cards float over his shoulder or take the full frame, one card per feature.
one_thing: Claude's mobile apps got a batch of upgrades (Duo/iPad artifact column, Android laptop mode, faster voice, 24 more languages), with search still to come.

transcript.voice_style: Warm, quick, conversational first-person; casual asides ('like myself', 'for me has been great'); about 200 words a minute with short pauses.
transcript.script_shape: Opens on a demo sentence, says 'plus one more still on the way', walks platforms in order, saves the unshipped search for last, then a Command-K tip and a comment request.

structure.frame0: Presenter mid-sentence in a warm window-lit room, a foldable-phone card with a '4,406' chart already floating at right from t=0.57s. Subject is present, not black.
structure.first_3s: Presenter says the chart line while the Duo card slides in at 0.57s, then a cream panel grows from the card to full frame at 2.8-3.0s.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Slow cuts (median 8.2s, longest 25.6s at 44.2-69.9s); movement comes from overlays, 30 appear events, card swaps and device draw-ons, plus the presenter's delivery. Cream card, presenter, cream card alternate.

look.ground: Warm off-white cream cards (luma 182) over a golden-hour presenter shot; dark charcoal ground for the voice and CarPlay section.
look.accent_use: Terracotta dot before each eyebrow label, the starburst, the underline on 'most requested', and the large '24'; one yellow bar marks the data point.
look.type: High-contrast serif display for titles, grotesque sans for labels, chips and UI; two-line titles, centred or left aligned on the card.
look.depth: Flat cards with soft shadows float over blurred live footage; the devices have light 3D hinge and shadow, nothing else has depth.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: No camera moves. The Duo hinge unfolds in 3D (3.4-4.4s), a card grows to full frame, and a dark panel zooms from a dot; otherwise UI is static.
product_ui.notes: Full-frame cards and titles read well; UI inside the small shoulder cards (f0001.jpg chart rows about 10px tall) and device screens at t=70-83s are too small. Product screens are designed, plausible mock UI with sample data, not captures.

motion.text_entry: Eyebrow, title and rows fade or rise in staggered; chips pop in one by one (f0004.jpg shows the fifth chip mid-fade); the Answers sooner. line fills in word by word.
motion.ui_motion: Typed input into the composer, chart bar changing 4,406 to 3,886 with a dashed ghost bar, waveforms animating, welcome card cycling languages, red outline highlight on the part being discussed.
motion.camera: Presenter shot is static; no push or pan on UI. Only the Duo hinge swing and the card-to-full-screen growth act as camera moves.
motion.eases: Soft ease-out on cards and a quick, snappy panel expansion in 0.2s (strip window-03); the device draw-on from dot to bar to screen takes about 0.8s.

good.observation: Every feature gets one card: eyebrow label, two-line serif title, one proof UI. Viewers can map the voice line to the card at a glance.
The opening shows the finished chart on a foldable at 0.57s and unfolds it by 4.4s, so the first 5s say what the update is.
Demo UI carries a story, not lorem ipsum: 'Drop week 12. Trade show.' changes 4,406 to 3,886 and the chart shows a dashed ghost bar.
A strict system keeps 21 on-screen lines consistent: cream cards, terracotta dots, serif title, sans caption, charcoal for audio features.
The big numeral '24' at 17.6% of frame height plus '33 in total' makes the statistic the picture.
Ending lands cleanly: comment prompt for about 3s, then the logo held 4.8s on plain cream.

weak.observation: A 25.6s shot (44.2-69.9s) is presenter with small overlays; the iPad/Duo UI inside is tiny and hard to read at phone width.
Several cream or grey blank panels hang for 0.3-1s between scenes before content arrives, which reads as an empty frame.
Device UI inside shoulder cards is about 10px tall, under the 2.6% floor, so the proof is mostly unreadable on a phone.

rule_candidates.rule: For a presenter film, put the proof card in the free right third from 0.5s and size it to at least 40% of frame height so the face and the product both read.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001.jpg card 370px tall of 720 at t=0.57s; f0007.jpg card 440px (61%).

rule_candidates.rule: In a presenter-led explainer, cut about every 8s and carry pace with overlay changes (about 30 appear events in 152s); a median shot of 1.8-3.5s is not needed for this format.
Title cards use a label line plus a title of at most 3 words per line over 2 lines, with a title line height of 5.7-8.6% of frame height.
Cause every scene change by the object on screen: grow the floating card to full frame, or draw the device from a dot-bar-screen in under 1s, so the cut never reads as a dissolve.
Close with a one-line prompt held at least 2s (here about 3s), then the logo on plain ground held about 5s.
Switch ground colour with the topic: dark charcoal cards for audio features, cream for visual ones, so a section change is readable without any caption.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0044.jpg, f0050.jpg versus f0040.jpg; section break at 83s and 106.9s.

rule_candidates.rule: Mix a speech-only soundtrack to -13 to -14 LUFS but keep true peak at or below -1 dBTP; this one peaks at -0.9, 0.1 dB over.
When a number is the claim, make the numeral the largest element (about 17% of frame height) and add a plain qualifier line beneath it.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0058.jpg '24 more languages', numeral 127px of 720; f0061.jpg '33 in total'.
